glossary.superficial veins: Veins just under the skin, above the deep fascia.
glossary.deep veins: Veins running within the muscles, which carry most blood back from the legs.
glossary.obesity: Excess body fat, usually a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.dorsum: The back or top surface; of the foot, the top.
glossary.femoral vein: Main deep vein of the thigh.
glossary.postero-lateral: Towards the back and outer side.
glossary.medial: Towards the midline of the body.
glossary.swelling: Enlargement of a body part, often from fluid (oedema).
glossary.quality of life: How much a condition affects a person's day-to-day wellbeing.
glossary.valve incompetence: Failure of vein valves to close, letting blood flow backwards.
glossary.leg elevation: Raising the legs above the heart to help venous drainage.
glossary.interventional: Treatment by a procedure rather than drugs or lifestyle.
glossary.RFA: Radiofrequency ablation, using heat from radio waves to close a vein.
glossary.sclerotherapy: Injecting a chemical into a vein to scar and close it.
glossary.contraindicated: Should not be given because it could cause harm in this patient.
glossary.PAD: Peripheral arterial disease, narrowing of the leg arteries by atherosclerosis.
glossary.peripheral arterial disease: Narrowing of the leg arteries, usually from atherosclerosis.
glossary.graduated compression stockings: Stockings tightest at the ankle and looser higher up, pushing blood back towards the heart.
glossary.gravity: The force pulling blood down towards the feet when standing.
glossary.competent: Working properly; competent valves stop backflow.
glossary.ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.arterial disease: Narrowing or blockage of arteries, usually from atherosclerosis.
glossary.pigmentation: Colouring of the skin, here brown from haemosiderin.
glossary.catheter: A thin tube passed into a vessel.
glossary.pregnancy: Raises venous pressure in the legs through hormones and pelvic vein compression.
